source.author: lucan
source.text: Quorum qui maximus aevo Aruns incoluit desertae moenia Lucae, Fulminis edoctus motus, venasque calentes Fibrarum, et monitus volitantis in aere pennae, Monstra iubet primum, nullo quae semine discors Protulerat natura, rapi, sterilique nefandos Ex utero fetus infaustis urere flammis.
source.text_original: Quorum qui maximus aevo / Aruns incoluit desertae moenia Lucae, / Fulminis edoctus motus, venasque calentes / Fibrarum, et monitus volitantis in aere pennae, / Monstra iubet primum, nullo quae semine discors / Protulerat natura, rapi, sterilique nefandos / Ex utero fetus infaustis urere flammis.
source.text_english: Of these, Aruns, the eldest in years, inhabited the walls of deserted Luca. Taught the movements of thunder and the warm veins of entrails and the warnings of a feather flying in the air, he first commands that monsters be seized, which nature, at variance and producing them from no seed, had brought forth, and that the accursed offspring be burned from the barren womb with baleful flames.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: sed non ulla quies animo fratrisque paventi progeniem divumque minas; hunc nam fore regi exitio vatesque canunt pecudumque per aras terrifici monitus iterant: super ipsius ingens instat fama viri virtusque haut laeta tyranno.
reuse.text_original: sed non ulla quies animo fratrisque paventi / progeniem divumque minas; hunc nam fore regi / exitio vatesque canunt pecudumque per aras / terrifici monitus iterant: super ipsius ingens / instat fama viri virtusque haut laeta tyranno.
reuse.text_english: but there was no rest for his mind, nor for his fearful brother, because of the offspring and the threats of the gods; for seers proclaim that this man will be the king’s destruction, and the dreadful warnings repeat themselves through the altars of the sacrificial beasts: over and above the man himself looms a great renown and a valor not pleasing to the tyrant.
